item: The registry names the SQLAlchemy functions the write-gate hold classifier looks for (sqlalchemy-phase-names), read on four releases
summary: src/database/writer.py _PHASE_AT names six SQLAlchemy functions (pool.impl._do_get, util.queue.get, engine.default.do_execute / do_executemany / do_execute_no_params / do_commit / do_rollback); a release that renames one makes a hold's phase read python and hides whether the holder waited for the pool. tests/test_write_gate_phase.py already failed on such an install; the registry now carries the coupling as its own block at the end of the file (the ruling), with a refresh recipe (unpacked wheel first on PYTHONPATH, run that file, extend the table, never loosen the test) and a row in EXTERNAL_DEPENDENCIES.md. Read on 2026-10-17 on 2.0.31, 2.0.51 (requirements.lock), 2.1.1 and 2.1.5 (the newest then): 10 of 10 pass on each. Found on the way: 2.0.30, the floor pyproject.toml names, does not import on Python 3.13 (TypeError in util/langhelpers.py: Can't replace canonical symbol for __firstlineno__), so the floor moves to 2.0.31 in pyproject.toml and the registry in this one commit (coordinator ruling, version coupling); requirements.lock pins 2.0.51 and needed no change (the lock-file install job reads neither the specifier nor a metadata hash of pyproject.toml), and a test pins registry floor = pyproject floor <= the lock pin. No upstream_check on purpose: SQLAlchemy tags releases rel_2_1_5, which the GitHub watch would read as different from 2.1.5 every week.
